units.title: 3.1 The human body and movement in physical activity and sport

outcomes.text: Name the key bones of the head, shoulder, chest, elbow, hip, knee and ankle.
Describe how bones, muscles and joints work together to affect health, fitness and performance.
Explain how the skeleton gives a framework for movement: bone shape, joints and muscle attachment.
List the skeleton's functions: support, protection, movement, shape, mineral storage and blood cell production.
Identify the main muscles of the body, from deltoid and biceps to gastrocnemius and tibialis anterior.
State that tendons attach muscle to bone.
Identify the parts of a synovial joint and how each helps prevent injury.
Match hinge joints (elbow, knee, ankle) and ball and socket joints (hip, shoulder) to their movements.
Link flexion, extension, abduction, adduction, rotation, circumduction and plantar/dorsiflexion to joints.
Explain agonist and antagonist pairs at major joints and concentric versus eccentric contractions.
Name the pathway of air from mouth and nose to the alveoli.
Explain how alveoli suit gas exchange: large area, thin moist walls, many capillaries, short diffusion path.
Describe how oxygen binds to haemoglobin and that haemoglobin can also carry carbon dioxide.
Compare arteries, capillaries and veins in size, wall thickness and valves.
Explain vasoconstriction and vasodilation in redistributing blood during exercise.
Name the chambers and main vessels of the heart.
Trace the pathway of blood and the cardiac cycle of diastole and systole.
Use cardiac output = stroke volume x heart rate and interpret heart rate graphs.
Describe the roles of intercostals, ribs and diaphragm in inhaling and exhaling at rest and in exercise.
Identify tidal, reserve and residual volumes on a spirometer trace and how they change in exercise.
Define aerobic and anaerobic exercise and give their word equations.
Match sporting activities to aerobic or anaerobic work by intensity and duration.
Define EPOC (oxygen debt) and link it to lactic acid from vigorous exercise.
Evaluate recovery methods: cool down, diet and rehydration, ice baths and massage.
Describe immediate effects of exercise: skin, breathing and heart rate changes.
Describe short-term effects such as fatigue, nausea and DOMS.
Describe long-term effects such as stronger muscles, a larger heart and lower resting heart rate.
Explain basic principles of movement and how they affect performance.
Identify first, second and third class levers and draw them showing fulcrum, load and effort.
Link levers to sporting actions at the elbow, knee and ankle.
Calculate mechanical advantage as effort arm divided by resistance arm.
Link movement types at joints to actions like push-ups, running, jumping and cricket bowling.
Identify frontal, transverse and sagittal planes and the three axes for sporting actions.
Plan, monitor and evaluate personal exercise and training programmes using principles of training.
Define health and fitness and explain how ill health can lower fitness.
Define agility, balance, cardiovascular endurance, coordination, flexibility, muscular endurance, power, reaction time, strength and speed.
Justify which components of fitness different sports need.
Give reasons for and limitations of fitness testing.
Describe the procedures of the named test for each component, such as multi-stage fitness test or sit and reach.
Explain how test data are recorded and compared with national averages.
Explain SPORT: specificity, progressive overload, reversibility and tedium.
Explain overload with FITT: frequency, intensity, time and type, and apply it to sport.
Describe circuit, continuous and fartlek training.
Describe interval, static stretching, weight and plyometric training.
Evaluate advantages and disadvantages of training types for specific aims and sports.
Define training threshold and calculate maximum heart rate and aerobic and anaerobic training zones.
Use one rep max for strength and muscular endurance training.
List the factors that prevent injury: warm up, avoiding over training, clothing, taping, hydration, technique, rest.
Describe high altitude training and evaluate its benefits and limits.
Describe pre-season, competition and post-season aims and apply them to sports.
Describe the parts of a warm up and its benefits.
Describe the parts of a cool down and its benefits.
Explain how data are used in physical activity and sport.
Distinguish quantitative from qualitative data and how each is collected.
Present data in tables, bar charts and line graphs with labelled axes.
Interpret data in tables, bar charts, line graphs and pie charts.

units.title: 3.2 Socio-cultural influences and wellbeing in physical activity and sport

outcomes.text: Describe psychological, social and health influences on physical activity and sport.
Explain psychological factors that affect performers.
Define skill and ability and classify skills as basic/complex, open/closed, self/externally paced, gross/fine.
Define performance and outcome goals and set targets for sporting examples.
Evaluate performance versus outcome goals, including for beginners.
Write SMART targets: specific, measurable, accepted, realistic, time bound.
Explain the input, decision making, output and feedback stages of the model.
Apply the model to sporting skills and draw it as a box diagram.
Evaluate visual, verbal, manual and mechanical guidance for beginners and elite performers.
Evaluate positive/negative, knowledge of results/performance and intrinsic/extrinsic feedback.
Define arousal and draw and explain the inverted-U theory.
Link optimal arousal to gross and fine skills.
Explain deep breathing, mental rehearsal and positive self-talk for controlling arousal.
Define direct and indirect aggression with sporting examples.
Describe introvert and extrovert personalities and the sports that suit them.
Define intrinsic and extrinsic motivation with sporting examples.
Evaluate the merits of intrinsic and extrinsic motivation.
Explain how social factors and commercialisation affect sport and society.
Explain how gender, culture, age, peers and disability affect participation.
Link factors like role models, access, media, stereotyping, leisure time and income to participation.
Define commercialisation and the link between sport, sponsorship and media.
Describe types of sponsorship and media.
Justify positive and negative impacts of sponsorship and media on performers, sport, officials, spectators and sponsors.
Justify positive and negative impacts of technology on performers, sport, officials, spectators and sponsors.
Define etiquette, sportsmanship, gamesmanship and contract to compete.
Name categories of prohibited substances and their effects and side effects.
Describe blood doping, its effects, side effects and who benefits.
Describe beta blockers: use, side effects and prescription.
Match each drug type to the performers who might use it.
Evaluate advantages and disadvantages of drug use for performers and sport.
Describe positive and negative effects of spectators at events.
Explain reasons for hooliganism and evaluate strategies to combat it.
Explain how participation benefits health, fitness and wellbeing.
Describe physical, mental, social and fitness benefits of participation for different people.
Define sedentary and lifestyle and list the consequences of inactivity.
Define obesity and explain its effect on performance and physical, mental and social health.
Define endomorph, mesomorph and ectomorph and match body types to sports.
Describe energy in Kcal and what affects daily requirements.
Explain the reasons for a balanced diet.
Describe roles and proportions of carbohydrate, fat, protein, vitamins and minerals.
Define dehydration and explain its effects on performance.
